structural_memory.memory: Shipboard freshwater service spans owner/manager, master, engineering crew, hotel/catering or accommodation users, shore technical or marine support, water-system equipment/service actors and port or shore water-supply actors. Source provision, onboard equipment condition, inventory custody, distribution and quality confidence can therefore belong to different responsibilities.

Freshwater source availability and onboard water inventory are separate states. Onboard production equipment or a shore-supply opportunity may be unavailable while stored inventory remains, and an available source does not prove that sufficient usable inventory has been produced or received.

Onboard production readiness and actual production are distinct lifecycle states. Equipment may be installed, available, degraded, unavailable or under support while observed water production is a separate event or interval; exact process, rate and treatment parameters are deferred.

Shore or port water supply has offer/availability, vessel acceptance/readiness, transfer indication, receipt and closure states. Those states do not by themselves establish water quality, exact quantity or regulatory suitability, which require claim-scoped Evidence.

Storage and inventory should preserve quantity-confidence and location/availability separately from source history. A historical replay benefits from knowing when inventory was believed available without turning blind Memory into tank-capacity, sounding, consumption or transfer calculations.

Intended-use separation is structurally useful: potable/domestic or accommodation use and selected technical uses should not be assumed interchangeable. The pass retains the existence of use-class distinctions while deferring exact vessel piping, tank assignments, cross-connections and suitability rules.

Freshwater demand/consumption and supply/production are separate clocks. A shortage can emerge from changing demand, reduced production, reduced shore access, uncertain inventory or distribution loss without any one factor being established as the root cause.

Shortage or degraded-availability has a lifecycle that can preserve observation, uncertain scope, service restriction or reduced availability, resupply/recovery expectation, restoration indication and verification. This is a state model only and contains no rationing or operating procedure.

Water quality confidence is separate from both quantity and confirmed contamination. Structural states can include normal confidence, concern or suspicion, evidence pending, restricted/isolated status, result or clearance indication and restored confidence without retaining thresholds, tests, organisms, treatment or health advice.

Distribution availability is distinct from source and storage availability. Water can exist onboard while an affected distribution segment or end-use service is unavailable, so downstream service loss should not automatically be attributed to production failure or depleted inventory.

Isolation should be represented as a bounded service state rather than a whole-vessel conclusion. A source, storage location or distribution segment may be treated as unavailable or segregated while other supply remains; exact valves, piping, procedures and reasons are deferred.

Freshwater degradation can propagate into accommodation, galley, sanitation and selected technical services, but simultaneous downstream problems are dependency observations rather than proof of a water-source, distribution or quality root cause.

Restoration should keep source/production return, inventory confidence, distribution return, end-use availability and quality-confidence clearance as potentially different timestamps. Resumed production or transfer alone does not establish complete freshwater-service recovery.

P070 electrical availability can be an upstream dependency for water production and distribution, but electrical power being present does not prove freshwater production, inventory, distribution or quality confidence.

P067 equipment lifecycle should keep watermaker, pump or treatment-equipment condition separate from freshwater service state. Healthy equipment can coexist with insufficient source/inventory or an isolated service, and water availability does not prove equipment condition.

Crew-welfare and accommodation outcomes should treat freshwater availability as one possible dependency rather than a complete welfare judgment; reduced service can matter while the cause and broader welfare effect remain separately evidenced.

Point-in-time replay should distinguish first onboard observation of a quality concern, any later sample/result or shore notification, and any later clearance. Later knowledge must not silently rewrite what the vessel or manager could have known earlier.
Equipment readiness, support, modification and restoration mechanics overlap the generic marine-equipment lifecycle recovered in P067.

Dependency propagation, degraded-service, isolation and verified-restoration mechanics overlap the digital, connectivity and electrical state models recovered in P068-P070; P071 applies them to freshwater service and quality confidence.

reviewed_no_specific_memory: Exact vessel water-system diagrams, tank assignments/capacities, production rates, consumption figures and transfer quantities are intentionally not retained.
Exact desalination, treatment, dosing, disinfection, sampling, microbiology, laboratory methods, water-quality thresholds and health interpretations are outside this blind pass.
Named water-system OEMs/service companies, laboratories, port water suppliers, vessel incidents, contamination findings and rule-specific compliance claims require claim-scoped Evidence.
Private/regional watermaker, treatment, laboratory, bunkering and port-water provider lineages plus historical non-English terminology remain deferred for source archaeology.
negative_space: Exact tank/piping topology, capacities, production rates, consumption quantities and transfer details.
Treatment, dosing, disinfection, sampling, microbiology, testing thresholds or health/consumption guidance.
Named suppliers, equipment, laboratories, vessel incidents, contamination findings, regulations and current readiness.
Private/regional freshwater-service lineages and non-English predecessor terminology.
epistemic_boundary: Memory-only defensive freshwater service-availability and quality-confidence orientation/source-discovery output. It is not potable-water, health, treatment, sampling, engineering, bunkering or vessel-operating advice and does not establish any exact capacity, rate, quantity, treatment parameter, test result, threshold, supplier, incident, contamination finding, compliance status or current-readiness fact.
stop_reason: The freshwater lifecycle is recalled at useful structural resolution: source/production, shore supply, inventory, intended use, demand, quality confidence, distribution, isolation and verified restoration are separable states. Further detail would become tank-, piping-, treatment-, sampling-, microbiology-, health-, vessel-, rule-, incident-, supplier- or jurisdiction-specific and is deferred to claim-scoped Evidence.
